name: Reaper::new / Reaper::sweep_orphans

test_list.description: A journaled registration appears in reaper.journal at once and is gone after release; an empty journal file is deleted.
After a fully successful shutdown_all the journal file does not exist.
A resource that was Failed or Abandoned remains in the journal for the next start-up.
After a simulated crash the next Reaper::new + sweep_orphans removes the leftover polaris-reaper- temp dir, reports Removed and clears the journal.
A journal cut in the middle of its last record yields the complete records and counts one ignored line.
A record present twice in the journal produces one orphan report.
A tampered journal pointing at a directory without the polaris-reaper- prefix is listed (NeedsOperator) but the directory is left alone.
A label containing tab and newline characters round-trips as one record and cannot inject a second record.
Pid and label records are returned as NeedsOperator (killing needs start-time verification in polaris-platform-process, P2); acknowledge_orphan removes them from the journal.
A journal with an unknown header makes Reaper::new fail rather than overwrite it.

dependencies: polaris_kernel_reaper::{Reaper, Locator, ResourceKind, OrphanAction, JOURNAL_FILE_NAME, TEMP_DIR_PREFIX}
output_description: One OrphanReport per leftover record plus the number of ignored lines.
